body.statement: There exists \(K_\alpha<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha,c,C_0,\mu,B,r_0,\sigma\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})]/w_n\le K_\alpha\).
body.justification: Coverage alone could be achieved by projection; transition-order expected length makes the interval informative at joint zero.
body.gap: Neither the panel anchor nor generic minimum-distance theory proves a donor-uniform expected-length bound at the sum of first- and second-order scales.
body.consumer: The bound supplies a principled uncertainty floor for entrywise treatment-effect reporting in strong-factor panels.
